## Onchocerciasis

<div class="disease-summary"><em>Onchocerca volvulus</em> causes skin disease and eye damage, including blindness.</div><div class="transmission-visual"><div><img src="assets/blackfly-icon.svg" alt="Blackfly vector"><h3>Blackflies <em>(Simulium)</em></h3><p>Vectors breed in fast-flowing rivers</p></div><div class="transmission-link"><span>⇄</span><p>Transmission through<br>blackfly bites</p></div><div><img src="assets/people-icon.svg" alt="People"><h3>People</h3><p>Infected people carry the parasite</p></div></div><div class="takeaway">Repeated ivermectin treatment aims to interrupt transmission.</div>



## What evidence supports stopping treatment?

<div class="assessment-intro">Evidence from people and vectors across the assessment area</div><div class="assessment-grid"><div class="assessment-card"><img src="assets/serology-icon.svg" alt="Blood sample, schematic"><h3>Epidemiological assessment</h3><p>Evidence of exposure to <em>O. volvulus</em> in children</p><p class="assay">Ov16 serology</p></div><div class="assessment-card"><img src="assets/pcr-icon.svg" alt="Laboratory tubes, schematic"><h3>Entomological assessment</h3><p>Evidence of infective parasites in blackflies</p><p class="assay">O-150 PCR pool screening</p></div></div><div class="decision-sequence"><span>Assess the evidence</span><b>→</b><span>Stop treatment when criteria are met</span><b>→</b><span>Post-treatment surveillance</span></div>

## Blackfly Finder: a two-part hurdle model {#the-collection-model-has-two-parts}

<div class="finder-components"><div><div class="component-symbol"><span class="zero-catch">0</span><span class="component-arrow">/</span><span class="positive-catch">+</span></div><h3>Will we find flies?</h3><p>Probability of a positive catch</p><div class="model-detail">Ensemble of presence models</div></div><div><div class="catch-bars"><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i></div><h3>How many might we collect?</h3><p>Expected catch when flies are found</p><div class="model-detail">Negative-binomial count model</div></div></div>
<div class="model-equation"><strong>Expected catch</strong><span>=</span><span>Probability of finding flies</span><span>×</span><span>Expected positive catch</span></div><div class="model-caution">Allows for differences in observation duration.</div>



## What informs Blackfly Finder?

<div class="predictor-grid merged-predictors">
<div><span class="predictor-mark turquoise">≈</span><h3>Rivers and terrain</h3><p>Hydrology and landscape shape</p></div>
<div><span class="predictor-mark orange">☀</span><h3>Climate</h3><p>Temperature and rainfall</p></div>
<div><span class="predictor-mark purple">≋</span><h3>Soils</h3><p>Soil properties and temperature</p></div>
<div><span class="predictor-mark blue">⌁</span><h3>Land and vegetation</h3><p>Land cover, population and livestock</p></div>
</div>

<div class="selection-components merged-components"><div><h3>Presence / absence</h3><p>Environmental inputs combined in<br>an ensemble of presence models</p></div><div><h3>Positive-catch intensity</h3><p>Air temperature range · soil clay content<br>Soil temperature seasonality · terrain variation</p></div></div>
<div class="model-caution selection-takeaway">Different predictors can explain where flies are found and how many are caught.</div>

## An adaptive strategy to test {#an-adaptive-plan-needs-a-field-test}

:::: {.strategy-rows}
::: {.strategy-row}
<div class="strategy-number">1</div>

::: {.strategy-text}
**Prepare original and reserve sites**

Use the same selection process for both.
:::
:::
::: {.strategy-row}
<div class="strategy-number">2</div>

::: {.strategy-text}
**Choose when to replace a site**

Compare **1–4 initial zero months**, accounting for season and start month.
:::
:::
::: {.strategy-row}
<div class="strategy-number">3</div>

::: {.strategy-text}
**Validate with parallel field sampling**

Follow original sites for **12 months** and sample reserves alongside them.<br>Compare fly yields over the same calendar months.
:::
:::
::::

## Backup: models and analysis datasets {.technical-backup}

| Analysis | Dataset and purpose |
|---|---|
| Blackfly Finder | 676 locations; total catch and observed duration |
| Observed seasonality | 664 sites; 7,513 site-months |
| Early versus later catches | 374 sites; first complete 12-month window |
| Adaptive scenarios | Latent zero propensity and monthly seasonal exponents |

The mapped model, descriptive analyses and adaptive scenarios answer different questions.



## Backup: the mapped hurdle distribution {.technical-backup}

Let Y be total fly catch at a site and p = P(Y > 0).

<div class="backup-equation">P(Y = 0) = 1 − p</div>
<div class="backup-equation">P(Y = y) = p · f<sub>NB</sub>(y; μ, θ) / [1 − f<sub>NB</sub>(0; μ, θ)], &nbsp; y ≥ 1</div>
<div class="backup-equation">E(Y) = p · μ / [1 − (θ / (θ + μ))<sup>θ</sup>]</div>

The positive-count distribution is zero-truncated. μ is the underlying negative-binomial mean, not the truncated mean.



## Backup: presence score and calibration {.technical-backup}

Candidate learners: elastic-net logistic regression, XGBoost and random forest.

<div class="backup-equation">q(x) = Σ<sub>j</sub> w<sub>j</sub> q<sub>j</sub>(x)</div>

Saved weights: elastic net **0**, XGBoost **0**, random forest **1**.

<div class="backup-equation">logit p(x) = −3.033 + 6.016 q(x)</div>

The mapped hurdle model applies this logistic regression to the saved prediction score.



## Backup: fitted random-forest presence score {.technical-backup}

**500 trees**, mtry = **4**, minimum node size = **10**, Gini splitting.

<div class="backup-var-columns"><pre>soilT_1_0_5cm_r

The saved prediction bundle retains these 22 environmental inputs and training medians for imputation.



## Backup: positive-catch model {.technical-backup}

<div class="backup-equation">log μ = log T + 2.173 − 0.581 x<sub>1</sub> + 1.029 x<sub>2</sub><br>− 0.273 x<sub>3</sub> − 0.281 x<sub>4</sub></div>

| Predictor | Retained input |
|---|---|
| x₁ | Mean diurnal air-temperature range |
| x₂ | Soil clay content |
| x₃ | Soil-temperature seasonality, 5–15 cm |
| x₄ | Terrain deviation scale |

T is the number of observed sampling months. NB dispersion θ ≈ **0.299**.



## Backup: validation and calibration limits {.technical-backup}

- Location-level cross-validation compares candidate hurdle models.
- Candidates are ranked by RMSE, then MAE and deviance.
- Base presence predictions are out of fold; weights and upstream selection reuse outcomes.
- The reliability diagram shows an isotonic curve and a 90% pointwise consistency region.

Validation in new geographic settings and prediction of exceptional catches remain important.



## Backup: empirical early–late comparison {.technical-backup}

| First 3 months | Positive catch in months 4–12 | No later catch |
|---|---:|---:|
| At least one fly | 78 / 83 = **94.0%** | 5 / 83 |
| Zero flies | 46 / 291 = **15.8%** | 245 / 291 |

One complete consecutive 12-month period per site. Missing months are excluded.

For k = 1–4, the right-hand figure conditions on k initial zero months and observes months k+1–12.



## Backup: learning from repeated zeros {.technical-backup}

Let X be a latent site probability of zero catch, with density f₀(x).

<div class="backup-equation">M(r) = E(X<sup>r</sup>) = ∫₀¹ x<sup>r</sup> f₀(x) dx</div>
<div class="backup-equation">f<sub>k</sub>(x | k zeros) = x<sup>k</sup> f₀(x) / M(k)</div>
<div class="backup-equation">P(next catch > 0 | k zeros) = 1 − M(k+1) / M(k)</div>

This non-seasonal model updates the site's latent productivity after observing zeros.



## Backup: seasonal adaptive scenario {.technical-backup}

For ecological zone z and calendar month t:

<div class="backup-equation">P(zero in month t | X, z) = X<sup>s<sub>z</sub>(t)</sup></div>
<div class="backup-equation">S<sub>k</sub> = Σ<sub>first k months</sub> s<sub>z</sub>(t)</div>
<div class="backup-equation">E(C<sub>stay</sub> | zeros) = ν Σ<sub>remaining t</sub> [1 − M(S<sub>k</sub> + s<sub>z</sub>(t)) / M(S<sub>k</sub>)]</div>
<div class="backup-equation">E(C<sub>replace</sub>) = ν Σ<sub>remaining t</sub> [1 − M(s<sub>z</sub>(t))]</div>

Both options use the same remaining calendar months.



## Backup: gains and sensitivity {.technical-backup}

<div class="backup-equation">Gain (%) = 100 · [E(C<sub>replace</sub>) − E(C<sub>stay</sub>)] / E(C<sub>stay</sub>)</div>

- Compare initial zero runs k = 1, 2, 3 or 4.
- Evaluate every calendar start month and ecological setting.
- Consider retaining the first replacement or applying the rule again.
- A coupled extension allows positive yield to depend on zero propensity.

The displayed three-zero-month gains are scenario results, not realised field gains.



## Backup: site selection and future inference {.technical-backup}

- Filter candidate sites by river, road and community access.
- Rank by predicted positivity and enforce minimum site separation.
- Check major-river representation in the initial design.
- Replacements should follow the original selection process.

The planned joint epi–ento model would combine human exposure and vector infectivity evidence. Its specification is future work.
